title: Weather and zero-shot forecasting models: backtest results for GB electricity demand (part 1 of 2)
note: Zenodo report by Andy Moran. Chronos-2, Timestral-209M, TimesFM 2.5 (zero-shot) and a weekly-lag regression get the same ECMWF day-ahead weather for GB national demand. 960-day backtest, 16 Mar 2024 to 31 Oct 2026. Weather cut error 34% (regression), 32%, 23%, 6%. Edge over the regression largely gone with weather. Plan frozen 10 Nov 2026 before scoring. Archive holds plan, lock, results.

title: AndyMoran/gb-foundation-model-tests (README)
note: Repository for both GB studies, MIT licence. First study (no weather, 1,035 days): Chronos-2 0.928 and Timestral 0.910 of the regression's error, TimesFM 2.5 1.009. Weights loaded at pinned revisions; README states Chronos-2 and TimesFM 2.5 are Apache 2.0, Timestral Modified MIT. weather_study/ holds the second study's plan, lock and results. Live window to 31 Mar 2027.

title: weather_study/RESULTS.md: Q1
note: Q1 (confirmatory): error with weather over error without, 960 days, MAE over the day's half-hours. Regression 0.658 (0.631-0.686), Chronos-2 0.683 (0.658-0.707), Timestral 0.773 (0.751-0.796), TimesFM 2.5 0.941 (0.913-0.968); each one-sided p under 0.0005 at level 0.0125. Block bootstrap, 7-day blocks, 2,000 draws, 90% intervals.

title: weather_study/RESULTS.md: Q3 and Q2
note: Q3 (descriptive estimate): model error over the regression's, both with weather. Chronos-2 0.966 (0.931-1.001), Timestral 1.074 (1.034-1.115), TimesFM 2.5 1.453 (1.394-1.510); without weather they were 0.932, 0.914, 1.017. Q2: weather closed 456 MW (414-500), 62%, of Chronos-2's gap to NESO, which still leads (about 700 vs 980 MW).

title: weather_study/RESULTS.md: inputs, E4, E5, limits
note: Inputs differ beyond weather: the regression has day-of-week, bank-holiday and Christmas terms and refits daily on a year; models see 8 weeks, no calendar (named a design oversight). E4, 925 ordinary days: Chronos-2 0.940 (0.907-0.971). E5 exploratory, Chronos-2 given the calendar too: 0.903 (0.871-0.933) of the regression; Timestral 1.087. Regression weather: temperature, its square, wind, solar.

title: weather_study/RESULTS.md: preregistration and leakage
note: Plan, code and inputs tagged weather-plan on 10 Nov 2026; backtest scored once on 11 Nov, passed 20 gate checks. Pinned revisions: chronos-2 29ec376, Timestral-209M 9874d25, timesfm-2.5 1d95242. Backtest overlaps possible training data; E1: on 367 days after Chronos-2's release (30 Oct 2025) its weather ratio is 0.664 vs 0.695 before. Live window reports April 2027.

title: weather_study/PLAN.md (analysis plan, frozen at tag weather-plan)
note: Plan agreed 8 Nov, amended 9 Nov, frozen 10 Nov 2026, stating no forecaster had yet been given real weather. Q1 (does weather help each forecaster) is the only confirmatory question, four tests at 0.0125. Q3 (edge over the regression with the same weather) is an estimate with interval, no test. Result sentences written in advance. Chronos-2 takes weather as past and future covariates.

title: amazon/chronos-2 model card
note: Card describes a 120M-parameter zero-shot model that natively takes past-only and known-future covariates, context up to 8192, prediction up to 1024 steps, CPU or GPU. Training data: subsets of Chronos Datasets and GIFT-Eval Pretrain plus synthetic data. The fetched text did not include the licence tag.

title: amazon/chronos-2 commit history
note: The commit that added the weights and config (95a9710) is dated 2025-10-30; all later commits are README or tag changes, the latest 29ec376 on 2026-06-05. The file listing shows model.safetensors last changed by that weights commit. So the weights predate our first scored week (2025-11-10).

title: amazon-science/chronos-forecasting (named by you-research, not fetched)
note: From the research call's source list: the Chronos code repository is under Apache-2.0 and its news dates the Chronos-2 release to 20 Oct 2025 (Hugging Face upload followed on 30 Oct 2025).

title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model (named by you-research, not fetched)
note: Related work, not a replication: on ISO New England and ENTSO-E load with weather and calendar covariates, zero-shot Chronos-2 did not match the best task-specific models; fine-tuning helped at short horizons. Known only from the research call's source snippet.

title: Explainable Load Forecasting with Covariate-Informed Time Series Foundation Models (named by you-research, not fetched)
note: Related work, not a replication: on TransnetBW (Germany) load, covariates improved Chronos-2's MAE by about 27%. Known only from the research call's source snippet.

title: you-research (standard): independent replication of the GB weather study
note: Search that found nothing: one standard research call, LinkedIn excluded, returned no independent replication of Moran's GB experiment. It named 11 sources: the record, RESULTS.md, PLAN.md, three model cards, the Chronos repo and release issue, and three related load studies with mixed results.
